ai.description: *Chirixalus simus* (Rhacophoridae) is a small frog (25–30 mm) with a pale brown or yellowish body. It features a dark interorbital triangle and distinct, expanded adhesive discs on its fingertips.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Chirixalus simus* is best distinguished by its distinct, dark brown X-shaped or hourglass marking on the dorsum, which is absent in most other similar Indian treefrogs.
ai.habitat: *Chirixalus simus* inhabits subtropical moist deciduous forests and wetlands in the Indian subcontinent, typically found on vegetation near water bodies at low to mid-altitudes.
ai.behavior: *Chirixalus simus* is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small insects among the vegetation surrounding its breeding pools.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Chirixalus simus* breeds during the monsoon, depositing foam nests containing approximately 100–200 eggs on vegetation overhanging water bodies.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Assam Asian Treefrog (*Chirixalus simus*) is found in Northeast India, specifically in Assam and West Bengal, typically inhabiting low-elevation wetlands and forests.
ai.callDescription: The Assam Asian Treefrog produces a series of short, high-pitched "peep" notes, typically heard from vegetation surrounding stagnant water bodies during the monsoon.
